meta.about: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited (GNFC), is a joint sector enterprise promoted by the Gujarat State Investments Limited (GSIL), a Government of Gujarat undertaking, and the Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd.(GSFC). The company was set up in Bharuch in 1976 while its manufacturing and marketing operations were started in 1982. The company operates businesses mainly in the Industrial Chemicals, Fertilizers apart from the small presence of IT services. In the chemical segment, it has a product portfolio of various bulk chemicals that are used in industries for manufacturing various specialty chemicals as well as end products.

The segment revenue declined 29% between FY22 and FY24, driven by lower realizations across all the products. [3] [4]

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for GNFC (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment-driven: Chemicals, Fertilisers and Others ((n)Code IT) each grow revenue and earn a segment result (EBIT) margin, as GNFC reports them; it does not disclose segment depreciation, so segment EBITDA cannot be built. The 'unallocated' line turns the sum of segment results into Screener EBITDA: it adds back depreciation and removes other income booked inside segments and head-office costs. Treasury (cash, bank deposits, G-secs, equity stakes and the inter-corporate deposits with Gujarat State Financial Services that Screener shows inside 'other assets') earns a yield; other income outside treasury is entered separately. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments._why: FY27 +18% (~Rs5,780 cr): Q1 Rs1,569 cr (+56% YoY, +5% QoQ) at war-time prices (TDI Rs255k/t vs Rs168k in Q3FY26); we assume ~Rs1,400 cr a quarter for Q2-Q4 as the war premium fades and acetic acid, ethyl acetate and Bharuch TDI lost run-days (Q2 starts with plants shut in July). FY28 -10% (~Rs5,200 cr): prices back to mid-cycle (FY25-26 normal run-rate ~Rs5,000 cr), the planned April-2027 Bharuch shutdown (the FY26 turnaround cost ~Rs375 cr of revenue) partly offset by ~Rs400 cr from WNA-III / AN melt-II from mid-2027. FY29 +18% (~Rs6,140 cr): first full year of the Rs2,800 cr projects (management 'ballpark' +Rs1,200-1,500 cr revenue at war prices; we take ~Rs1,000 cr) and ~4% on the base.
segments._marginWhy: Segment result margin 5.9% (FY20), 26.5% (FY21), 37.1% (FY22), 28.5% (FY23), 11.5% (FY24), 13.6% (FY25), 18.6% (FY26: 13.2% for Q1-Q3, 30.9% in Q4); Q1FY27 27.1%. FY27 19.5% = Q1 27% and ~17% for Q2-Q4. FY28 16%: between the FY24-25 trough (12.5%) and the FY20-26 median (18.6%), helped by CCPP savings (~Rs80-120 cr a year, ~1.5-2 pts) and hurt by the April-2027 shutdown (~Rs150 cr of profit in FY26's turnaround). FY29 17%: new nitric acid / AN capacity and no shutdown. Global TDI oversupply and Chinese scale cap the margin well below the FY21-23 boom.

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments._why: Urea (~Rs2,045 cr in FY26) and ANP (Rs719 cr). FY27 +8.5% (~Rs3,000 cr): higher gas and energy costs are passed into urea subsidy revenue and the Kharif-2026 NBS rate for ANP is ~10% higher (N Rs47.32/kg, P Rs52.76/kg); Q1 Rs649 cr (+12% YoY). FY28 -5%: April-2027 Bharuch shutdown and lower energy pass-through. FY29 +5%: volumes back, ~2-3% price.
segments._marginWhy: Loss in every year since FY21: -1.4% (FY21), -3.7%, -4.4%, -8.0%, -6.2%, -6.8% (FY26, Rs-187 cr; ANP alone Rs-40 cr). Q1FY27 -13.1% (Rs-85 cr), the seasonal low. FY27 -5.0% (~Rs-150 cr) includes the ~Rs61 cr energy-norm arrears (Apr-25 to Jun-26) booked in Q2FY27 and ~Rs49 cr a year of ongoing benefit from the 6.37 Gcal/t norm. FY28 -4.5%, FY29 -4.0%: no fixed-cost revision assumed (management: 'almost no chance' of urea profits until it comes).

assumptions._unallocLabel: Reconciliation: depreciation added back, less other income booked in segments and head-office costs (sum of segment results − EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Screener EBITDA = sum of segment results + depreciation − other income booked inside segments − unallocable expenses. FY26: 773 + 307 − 140 − 60 = 879; FY25: 508 + 303 − 140 − 56 = 615. Forecast: depreciation from the model (Rs335 / 378 / 402 cr) less other income in segments (~Rs90 cr: ASGP grant income Rs61 cr + recurring misc. ~Rs30 cr; one-offs such as insurance claims left out) less head-office costs (Rs62 / 65 / 68 cr) = −183 / −223 / −244. Engine workaround: if capex (and so depreciation) is changed in the Excel model, this line should be changed with it.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27: Rs300 cr in Q1 plus 'another Rs1,200-1,500 cr' (Aug-2026 call), i.e. Rs1,500-1,800 cr; we use Rs1,600 cr (the May-2026 figure of ~Rs2,800 cr was cut). FY28: the rest of the Rs2,800 cr project list (WNA-III Rs1,420 cr, AN melt-II, ammonia loop, CCPP Rs613 cr; ~Rs1,500 cr to spend 'over the next 2 years') plus the Rs480-500 cr boiler: Rs800 cr. FY29: maintenance (~Rs200 cr a year) and the boiler: Rs500 cr. Not included: BPA, polyols and acetic acid projects under study (BPA plus phenol ~Rs7,000-8,000 cr), decision expected by end-2026.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs307 cr = 3.6% of average gross block (Rs8,469 cr); Q1FY27 Rs76 cr. The engine depreciates capex at once while most of it sits in CWIP until mid-2027; 3.6% gives Rs335 cr in FY27 (Q1 run-rate plus the CCPP from Q2) and Rs378 / 402 cr in FY28-29, slightly low once the projects are capitalised.

otherTreasury._why: Deposits with a body corporate (inter-corporate deposits with Gujarat State Financial Services, a Government of Gujarat finance company) of Rs2,410 cr at Mar-26 (Rs545 cr at Mar-25), AR FY26 consolidated note 9. Screener shows them inside 'Loans n Advances' (other assets); they are surplus treasury, not working capital (CFO, May-2026 call: parked 'with the best yield ... till the time our capex cycle is over', ~7.25%).

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening treasury: cash and bank Rs1,109 cr + Screener investments Rs1,693 cr (G-secs Rs695 cr, equity stakes Rs998 cr incl. GSFC, Gujarat Alkalies, Gujarat Gas, Gujarat Chemical Port and the GGRC associate) + ICDs Rs2,410 cr − borrowings Rs5 cr = Rs5,207 cr at Mar-26. FY26 interest Rs313 cr + dividends Rs24 cr = Rs337 cr on ~Rs5,130 cr average (6.6%). We use 6.0%: deposit rates fell after the 2025 rate cuts, ~Rs1,000 cr of the base is equity yielding ~2.4%, and Q1FY27 other income (Rs101 cr) points to ~Rs300 cr a year of treasury income. The interest-bearing book (~Rs4,200 cr) earns ~6.9%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income, built from AR FY26 note 28: amortised ASGP government grant Rs61 cr a year (deferred grant balance Rs455 cr, so it runs to ~FY33; non-cash), recurring miscellaneous income ~Rs30 cr (Rs29 cr FY25, Rs47 cr FY26 incl. one-offs), lease rental Rs9 cr, plus the GGRC associate share (~Rs12 cr, after tax on Screener). One-offs left out: insurance (Rs29 cr FY26), FX gains (Rs13 cr), write-backs (Rs3 cr FY26, Rs51 cr FY25). FY27E total other income ~Rs424 cr vs Rs499 cr in FY26 and Rs450 cr TTM (to Q1FY27): the gap is the one-offs (~Rs45 cr) and a lower yield on a treasury that shrinks as capex is paid.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs6 cr, Q1FY27 Rs2 cr; borrowings Rs5 cr (leases) at Mar-26. Capex is funded from treasury.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 25.1% (statutory 25.17%, AR FY26 note 26); Q1FY27 25%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs18 (FY25, 44% of EPS) and Rs21 (FY26, 38%); Rs30 for FY23 (32%). We assume 35% while capex is heavy.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, so the cost of equity is the discount rate. Commodity chemicals with a state promoter and volatile earnings: beta 1.1, Ke 13.1%.
dcf._tgWhy: Fertiliser and bulk-chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; Chinese oversupply caps price growth: 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from the FY29E project-led 13% to 5% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 12%, GNFC's median for FY16-FY26 (mean 14.5%; range 6% in FY24 to 28% in FY22).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 5% of revenue (maintenance ~Rs200 cr plus periodic debottlenecking); depreciation 4.2% of revenue (FY26 3.9%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Middle East conflict keeps TDI, AN and acetic acid tight into FY28; the new nitric acid and AN capacity earns what management expects (Rs500-600 cr of contribution); the government revises urea fixed costs. Chemicals margin ~20-21%, fertiliser loss halves; P/E 10x (the own-history median without the FY23 peak and without the sector de-rating).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The war premium disappears, Chinese TDI and acetic acid flood Asia again and margins return to the FY24-25 trough (chemicals ~12-13%); the April-2027 shutdown runs long and fertiliser losses widen. P/E 6x (the low of the stock's forward P/E in the year before the war).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values GNFC: P/E on forward EPS (HDFC Securities's last full note used 6.5x FY24E). 7.5x = GNFC's 8.0x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian, leaving out the FY24-FY25 trough years), cut by the ~7% median de-rating of five fertiliser and commodity-chemical peers (GSFC, Chambal, Deepak Fertilisers, DCM Shriram, GHCL) against their five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (7.4x, rounded to 7.5x). No growth premium: Sep-28E EPS is no higher than FY26. Bull 10x (the median without the FY23 peak year and without the de-rating); bear 6x (the low of the stock's forward P/E in the year before the war, 5.9x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts the treasury at full value and asks what the market has paid for the operations. GNFC's median forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 2.0x leaving out trough years (FY24-26; 3.9x on all dates; EV = market value + debt − cash, investments and ICDs), cut by the ~9% median EV/EBITDA de-rating of seven peers (1.8x, rounded to 2x). Bull 4x (the all-dates median), bear 1.5x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests the cash flows with full credit for the treasury: 15-year FCFF, Ke 13.1%, terminal growth 5%, EBITDA margin fading to the 12% FY16-26 median.

cover.headline: A war windfall priced as if it will last: initiate with SELL
cover.lead: GNFC is India's only TDI maker and a debt-free state company with ~₹5,207 cr of treasury (₹354 a share). Since the US-Iran war began in late February 2026, chemical prices have spiked: chemicals EBIT was ₹463 cr in Q4FY26 and ₹425 cr in Q1FY27, against ~₹150 cr a quarter before, and the stock is up ~65% from its March low. We think most of that is a windfall: GNFC itself says global TDI capacity exceeds demand and that the war "can go either side". We value GNFC the way the street does, on **P/E of Sep-28E earnings**, at **7.5x** (its own 8.0x ex-trough forward median cut by the 7% sector de-rating). That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** The cash is real, but the market has never given GNFC full credit for it, and the state decides how it is spent. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}} (the war premium lasts into FY28); bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The war is doing the work
arguments.p: TDI rose from ₹168k a tonne (Q3FY26) to ₹255k (Q1FY27) and every spread GNFC tracks widened. The same war lifted fuel oil (+76% QoQ) and gas (+64%) costs and forced acetic acid, ethyl acetate and part of TDI to shut. Chemicals margin was 13% in the nine months before the war and 27-31% since. We assume it fades to 16-17%.

arguments.h: Strip out the war and earnings are flat
arguments.p: Our Sep-28E EPS of ₹55.2 equals FY26's ₹55.0 and is well below the TTM ₹70.6. New ammonium nitrate and nitric acid capacity (mid-2027) and a coal-fired steam plant help; prices normalising, a planned April-2027 shutdown and lower treasury income hurt. FY24-25 EPS was ₹34-41.

The segment lost ₹187 cr in FY26 and ₹85 cr in Q1FY27. A higher urea energy norm adds ~₹49 cr a year (plus ~₹61 cr of arrears in Q2FY27), but the fixed-cost revision has not come and management sees "almost no chance" of urea profits without it. We model losses of ₹120-150 cr a year.

arguments.h: The cash is real, but it is not yours
arguments.p: ₹2,410 cr of the treasury is lent to a state finance company at ~7.25%; a ₹7,000-8,000 cr BPA/phenol idea is under study; GNFC has had four MDs since Feb-2025. At ₹604 the market pays 7.1x operating earnings net of cash; at the March-2026 low it paid almost nothing. Our DCF (₹877) is the value only if the cash came back to shareholders.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): chemical margins after the July shutdowns, the ~₹61 cr energy-norm arrears and how much of the Q1 inventory was sold at war-time prices.
The Middle East conflict and oil (Brent ~US$103 on 29-Sep-2026): a ceasefire would cut both GNFC's prices and its fuel costs, and probably the former faster.
Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates (not announced by 30-Sep-2026) and any urea fixed-cost revision.
Board decision on BPA, polyols and the 350 KTPA acetic acid plant, expected by end-2026.
WNA-III, AN melt-II and the ammonia loop around mid-2027; planned Bharuch shutdown in April 2027; China/Japan/Korea TDI anti-dumping duty expires in September 2027.

sections.title: A state-owned chemical complex with a regulated fertiliser plant attached

blocks.p: GNFC runs two integrated complexes in Gujarat: Bharuch (since 1982) and Dahej (TDI-II, since 2014). It turns fuel oil, natural gas, coal, toluene, benzene and methanol into ammonia and syngas, and those into fertilisers and about a dozen bulk chemicals. Fertilisers (neem-coated urea and ANP) are 36% of revenue but sold at government-fixed prices with a subsidy; chemicals are 63% of revenue and sold at import-parity prices on one- to three-month contracts. A small IT division, (n)Code Solutions, makes up "Others". The Government of Gujarat (through Gujarat State Investments) and GSFC own 41.3%.

sections.title: China sets the price of almost everything GNFC sells; the war lifted it for now

blocks.p: GNFC's chemicals are commodities. TDI, aniline, acetic acid and methanol trade at one Asian price, and China, with plants several times GNFC's size running on cheap coal, is the marginal supplier. GNFC prices at import parity (the landed cost of imports, including any anti-dumping duty), so its realisations rise and fall with Chinese prices and the rupee. Between FY22 and FY26 its TDI price fell from ₹229k a tonne (FY23) to ₹173k, its aniline-benzene spread from ₹77k to ₹44k and its acetic acid-methanol spread from ₹45k (FY22) to ₹7k. Then the US-Iran war, from late February 2026, disrupted Gulf supply and shipping: TDI jumped to ₹255k a tonne in Q1FY27 and every spread GNFC tracks widened, while fuel oil (+76% QoQ) and gas (+64%) costs also jumped.

sections.title: Chemicals: a good TDI franchise in a bad neighbourhood, now enjoying a war

blocks.p: Chemicals earned ₹913 cr of EBIT on ₹4,899 cr of revenue in FY26 (18.6%), but ₹463 cr of that came in the war-hit March quarter; the first nine months earned ₹450 cr (13.2%), close to FY24-25 (11.5-13.6%). TDI is the core: GNFC is the only producer in South Asia, makes ~57 kt a year across two plants (TDI-II at 77% utilisation in FY26) and sells ~60% of India's needs. In Q1FY27 revenue rose to ₹1,569 cr and EBIT to ₹425 cr (27.1%) on record prices, even though acetic acid (6-May to 1-Aug), ethyl acetate and part of TDI were shut because the feedstock cost more than the product was worth, and sales lagged production so inventory built up.

bullets: **TDI economics:** management said in Aug-2025 that TDI-II "does not fully recover" its fixed costs at recent prices. The coal-fired steam and power plant (CCPP, ₹613 cr) was supplying steam by the August 2026 call and should cut TDI-II costs by ₹30-40k a tonne at current gas and coal prices. That fixes part of the cost problem; it does not fix the price problem.
**Aniline:** uneconomic on its own against Chinese aniline made with coal-based hydrogen at 7-8x the scale; GNFC mostly processes it for other companies on a fixed margin.

**Acetic acid and methanol:** GNFC's methanol plants have been idle since Nov-2024 because gas is too expensive; it buys methanol or acetic acid, whichever is cheaper, to keep ethyl acetate running. Spreads were ₹7-12k a tonne through FY26.
**Ammonium nitrate and nitric acid:** the growth leg. AN prices rose ~20% QoQ in Q4FY26; AN melt-II and WNA-III double AN capacity from mid-2027.
**Technical-grade urea:** a quiet winner. When the war cut diesel-exhaust-fluid supply in March 2026, GNFC doubled TGU output; TGU was "one of the significant contributors" to Q1 profit.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** we model chemicals revenue +18% in FY27E (Q1 at war prices, ~₹1,400 cr a quarter after), −10% in FY28E (prices normalise; the April-2027 Bharuch shutdown) and +18% in FY29E (first full year of the new AN and nitric acid capacity). EBIT margin 19.5% / 16% / 17%: well below the last two quarters (27-31%) and the FY22 peak (37%), but above the FY24-25 trough (12.5%) because of CCPP savings and new capacity. Sep-28E chemicals EBIT of ₹938 cr compares with ₹665 cr in FY25 and ₹913 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Fertilisers: regulated, loss-making for six years, waiting on Delhi

blocks.p: GNFC makes neem-coated urea (reassessed capacity 637 kt; ~620 kt sold in FY26) and ANP, a 20:20:0 nitrogen-phosphate fertiliser (172,995 t). Neither price is set by the market. Urea sells at a fixed farm price and the government pays the rest of a "normative" cost under the New Urea Policy: gas at the pooled price, energy up to a plant-specific norm (Gcal per tonne) and a fixed-cost element. ANP gets a per-kg Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) set each season. In FY26 the segment had revenue of ₹2,764 cr, including ₹1,982 cr of subsidy, and lost ₹187 cr: about ₹147 cr on urea and ₹40 cr on ANP.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** GNFC has a protected position in Indian TDI and the advantages of an integrated, debt-free complex, but no moat that protects profits. It is a price-taker against much larger Chinese producers in every chemical it sells, and its fertiliser business earns whatever the government allows. Pre-tax returns on operating capital of ~15% in FY26 (helped by the war) and ~6-9% in FY24-25 are the evidence.

sections.title: A boom, a bust and a war: ten years of earnings that follow chemical prices

blocks.p: GNFC's revenue was ₹4,552 cr in FY16 and ₹7,773 cr in FY26: about 5.5% a year, with almost all of the growth in one jump (FY22-23) when Chinese supply was disrupted after COVID. EBITDA (operating profit before other income) swung from ₹361 cr (FY17) to ₹2,384 cr (FY22) and back to ₹502 cr (FY24). Net profit followed: ₹1,710 cr at the FY22 peak, ₹497 cr in FY24 and ₹809 cr in FY26, of which ₹396 cr came in the single war-hit March quarter. The only loss in fifty years was FY15 (₹443 cr), the year TDI-II started on borrowed money.

blocks.callout: **So what:** GNFC is a price-taker. Its profit is set by the gap between chemical prices (TDI, aniline, acetic acid, nitric acid) and feedstock costs (toluene, benzene, methanol, fuel oil, gas, coal), and Chinese supply sets both. Other income from its treasury (₹499 cr in FY26, 47% of pre-tax profit) steadies the bottom line. FY22-23 was a boom, FY24-25 a trough, and Q4FY26-Q1FY27 is a war spike: none of the three is a good base for valuation.

sections.title: Ten years of cash: debt repaid, a buyback, and ₹5,200 cr parked

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 GNFC generated ₹10,765 cr of operating cash. It spent only ₹2,153 cr on plants (it built nothing large between TDI-II in 2014 and the current projects), repaid ₹3,096 cr of debt, paid ₹1,714 cr of dividends and bought back ₹653 cr of shares in Dec-2023 at ₹770. The rest piled up: treasury (cash, deposits, G-secs, equity stakes and inter-corporate deposits) reached ~₹5,200 cr at March 2026, about ₹354 a share. Returns followed the chemical cycle: Screener's ROCE was 33% in FY22 and 12% in FY26 (diluted by the treasury); on operating capital alone the FY26 pre-tax return was ~15%, only slightly above a ~13% cost of equity, and that was helped by the war-time March quarter.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean books, but other income is half of pre-tax profit

bullets: **Other income is half of pre-tax profit.** FY26 other income was ₹499 cr against PBT of ₹1,065 cr: interest ₹313 cr, dividends ₹24 cr, a non-cash government grant amortisation ₹61 cr (the deferred ASGP grant, ₹455 cr left), insurance ₹29 cr, FX ₹13 cr and miscellaneous ₹47 cr. In FY24 and FY25 other income was 72% and 63% of PBT.

**One-offs every year.** Management counted ~₹80 cr of one-time income in FY26 (insurance, urea freight escalation, catalyst-dust sale, a penalty from the CCPP contractor) and ~₹38 cr in FY25. FY27 will include ~₹61 cr of energy-norm arrears for FY26 and Q1FY27.
**Subsidy accounting.** Urea subsidy is booked on estimates of the normative cost and trued up later ("escalation/de-escalation"): +₹8 cr for earlier years in FY26, −₹35 cr in FY25.
**Inventory timing.** In Q1FY27 production ran ahead of sales at record prices; ~15% of that stock was sold by end-July at "mixed" realisations.
**Treasury classification.** ₹2,410 cr of ICDs with a state finance company sit in "loans and advances", so Screener's cash line understates treasury by that amount.
**Audit.** Suresh Surana & Associates (statutory) and K. G. Goyal (cost); clean opinions; simple structure (one associate, no subsidiaries of size).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN, with a quality caveat.** We found nothing aggressive. But headline EPS mixes three things: chemical spreads, treasury income and one-offs. Our estimates strip one-offs from other income (₹112 cr a year of non-treasury income, mostly the grant) and grow treasury income only with the cash balance.

blocks.p: GNFC has had no meaningful debt since FY21. Adding them back, treasury rose slightly, to ~₹5,200 cr. About ₹1,000 cr of it is equity stakes in other Gujarat state companies (Gujarat Gas, Gujarat Alkalies, GSFC, Gujarat Chemical Port) and the GGRC associate, which earn dividends, not interest.

FY28 -10% (~Rs5,200 cr): prices back to mid-cycle (FY25-26 normal run-rate ~Rs5,000 cr), the planned April-2027 Bharuch shutdown (the FY26 turnaround cost ~Rs375 cr of revenue) partly offset by ~Rs400 cr from WNA-III / AN melt-II from mid-2027. FY29 +18% (~Rs6,140 cr): first full year of the Rs2,800 cr projects (management 'ballpark' +Rs1,200-1,500 cr revenue at war prices; we take ~Rs1,000 cr) and ~4% on the base.
segments._marginWhy: Segment result margin 5.9% (FY20), 26.5% (FY21), 37.1% (FY22), 28.5% (FY23), 11.5% (FY24), 13.6% (FY25), 18.6% (FY26: 13.2% for Q1-Q3, 30.9% in Q4); Q1FY27 27.1%. FY27 19.5% = Q1 27% and ~17% for Q2-Q4. FY29 17%: new nitric acid / AN capacity and no shutdown. Global TDI oversupply and Chinese scale cap the margin well below the FY21-23 boom.

FY27 +8.5% (~Rs3,000 cr): higher gas and energy costs are passed into urea subsidy revenue and the Kharif-2026 NBS rate for ANP is ~10% higher (N Rs47.32/kg, P Rs52.76/kg); Q1 Rs649 cr (+12% YoY). assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income, built from AR FY26 note 28: amortised ASGP government grant Rs61 cr a year (deferred grant balance Rs455 cr, so it runs to ~FY33; non-cash), recurring miscellaneous income ~Rs30 cr (Rs29 cr FY25, Rs47 cr FY26 incl. one-offs), lease rental Rs9 cr, plus the GGRC associate share (~Rs12 cr, after tax on Screener). One-offs left out: insurance (Rs29 cr FY26), FX gains (Rs13 cr), write-backs (Rs3 cr FY26, Rs51 cr FY25). FY27E total other income ~Rs424 cr vs Rs499 cr in FY26 and Rs450 cr TTM (to Q1FY27): the gap is the one-offs (~Rs45 cr) and a lower yield on a treasury that shrinks as capex is paid.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs6 cr, Q1FY27 Rs2 cr; borrowings Rs5 cr (leases) at Mar-26. Capex is funded from treasury.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 25.1% (statutory 25.17%, AR FY26 note 26); Q1FY27 25%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs18 (FY25, 44% of EPS) and Rs21 (FY26, 38%); Rs30 for FY23 (32%). We assume 35% while capex is heavy.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free, so the cost of equity is the discount rate. Commodity chemicals with a state promoter and volatile earnings: beta 1.1, Ke 13.1%.
dcf._tgWhy: Fertiliser and bulk-chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; Chinese oversupply caps price growth: 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from the FY29E project-led 13% to 5% by year 15.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades to 12%, GNFC's median for FY16-FY26 (mean 14.5%; range 6% in FY24 to 28% in FY22).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 5% of revenue (maintenance ~Rs200 cr plus periodic debottlenecking); depreciation 4.2% of revenue (FY26 3.9%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Middle East conflict keeps TDI, AN and acetic acid tight into FY28; the new nitric acid and AN capacity earns what management expects (Rs500-600 cr of contribution); the government revises urea fixed costs. Chemicals margin ~20-21%, fertiliser loss halves; P/E 10x (the own-history median without the FY23 peak and without the sector de-rating).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The war premium disappears, Chinese TDI and acetic acid flood Asia again and margins return to the FY24-25 trough (chemicals ~12-13%); the April-2027 shutdown runs long and fertiliser losses widen. P/E 6x (the low of the stock's forward P/E in the year before the war).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values GNFC: P/E on forward EPS (HDFC Securities's last full note used 6.5x FY24E). 7.5x = GNFC's 8.0x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian, leaving out the FY24-FY25 trough years), cut by the ~7% median de-rating of five fertiliser and commodity-chemical peers (GSFC, Chambal, Deepak Fertilisers, DCM Shriram, GHCL) against their five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (7.4x, rounded to 7.5x). No growth premium: Sep-28E EPS is no higher than FY26. Bull 10x (the median without the FY23 peak year and without the de-rating); bear 6x (the low of the stock's forward P/E in the year before the war, 5.9x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts the treasury at full value and asks what the market has paid for the operations. GNFC's median forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 is 2.0x leaving out trough years (FY24-26; 3.9x on all dates; EV = market value + debt − cash, investments and ICDs), cut by the ~9% median EV/EBITDA de-rating of seven peers (1.8x, rounded to 2x). Bull 4x (the all-dates median), bear 1.5x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests the cash flows with full credit for the treasury: 15-year FCFF, Ke 13.1%, terminal growth 5%, EBITDA margin fading to the 12% FY16-26 median.
